LESSON: READING 5.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: FICTION AND NON FICTION MATERIALS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.2: Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What materials do you enjoy reading?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a variety of materials for fluency

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 5.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: FICTION AND NON FICTION MATERIALS
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 5.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: FICTION AND NON FICTION MATERIALS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read a variety of materials for fluency

What this means
In this part you learn to read a variety of materials for fluency. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read a variety of materials for fluency.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read a variety of materials for fluency. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read a variety of materials for fluency)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read a variety of materials for fluency.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What materials do you enjoy reading?
2. Why is it necessary to read many books?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read a variety of materials for fluency.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
